publication_boundary: Verified public service information only. Legal-information and navigation records do not promise representation or provide legal advice.

records.name: BC Human Rights Clinic
records.description: Free initial legal advice about B.C. human-rights concerns, with representation available for eligible complaints that have been accepted and are proceeding at the Tribunal; separate intake is available for possible judicial review.
records.population_served: People with a provincial human-rights concern in British Columbia, subject to the clinic's current service criteria
records.eligibility: A free initial appointment is available for advice. Representation requires an accepted complaint that is proceeding at the B.C. Human Rights Tribunal and the clinic's intake approval.
records.access_pathway: Use the clinic appointment or representation intake on the current service page. Judicial-review help has a separate intake.

legal_support.representation: Representation is not automatic; it is available only for eligible accepted complaints selected through the clinic's intake.

records.name: Mental Health Law Program
records.description: Legal representation for people involuntarily detained under British Columbia's Mental Health Act or subject to the mental-disorder provisions of the Criminal Code.
records.population_served: People within the program's mental-health detention or Criminal Code mental-disorder mandate
records.eligibility: The person must fall within the program's stated involuntary-detention or Criminal Code mental-disorder mandate.
records.access_pathway: Review the current program information and contact CLAS for intake or referral guidance.

legal_support.representation: Representation is offered within the program's defined statutory mandate and intake process.

records.name: Virtual Indigenous Justice Centre
records.description: No-cost virtual legal advice, representation and referral services for Indigenous people across British Columbia, with lawyer bookings focused on criminal and child-protection matters.
records.population_served: Indigenous people with a legal matter in British Columbia, including people in communities without an in-person Indigenous Justice Centre
records.eligibility: Callers must self-identify as Indigenous, have a matter in British Columbia and be able to connect by phone. Free lawyer bookings focus on criminal and child-protection matters; other callers may receive information or referral help.
records.access_pathway: Call the toll-free intake line for navigation and a possible appointment with a lawyer.

legal_support.representation: Free representation is available within the centre's current criminal and child-protection mandate; other matters may receive information or referrals.

records.name: Police Accountability Unit
records.description: Indigenous-led legal support for eligible police-accountability matters in British Columbia, including navigation of complaint and oversight processes.
records.population_served: Indigenous people in British Columbia with a police-accountability concern within the unit's current mandate
records.eligibility: The concern must fit the unit's current police-accountability mandate and intake criteria.
records.access_pathway: Review the current mandate and contact the unit through its official intake page.

legal_support.representation: Service and representation depend on mandate, eligibility and intake capacity.

records.name: Alberta Human Rights Complaint Navigation
records.description: Official information and intake for complaints alleging discrimination within Alberta human-rights jurisdiction.
records.population_served: People considering a complaint under the Alberta Human Rights Act
records.eligibility: The complaint must fall within the Act and generally be made within one year of the alleged discriminatory act. Acceptance is not a finding on the merits.
records.access_pathway: Review the Commission's complaint guidance and submit through the official intake process.

legal_support.representation: The Commission provides process information and complaint administration, not private legal representation or individualized legal advice.

records.name: Alberta Ombudsman Complaint Review
records.description: Independent administrative-fairness review after available appeal or complaint routes have been used, including defined provincial health, professional-regulatory and benefit matters.
records.population_served: People with an administrative-fairness concern involving a body within the Alberta Ombudsman's jurisdiction
records.eligibility: Available complaint and appeal routes normally must be completed first. The office does not act as an advocate or court and does not investigate police conduct.
records.access_pathway: Use the jurisdiction checklist, complete other available review routes, then file through the Ombudsman's complaint process.

legal_support.representation: Independent review and recommendation role; not advocacy or legal representation.

records.name: Legal Aid Alberta
records.description: Application pathway for financially eligible Albertans seeking covered criminal, family or civil legal services.
records.population_served: People in Alberta who meet current financial, legal-issue and merit criteria
records.eligibility: Eligibility depends on current income and assets, the type of legal problem, and the merits and coverage rules for the service requested.
records.access_pathway: Apply through the current Legal Aid Alberta application process and provide the requested financial and case information.

legal_support.representation: A lawyer is provided only when the application is approved under current coverage and eligibility rules.

records.name: Residential Tenancy Dispute Resolution Service
records.description: Quasi-judicial dispute-resolution process for eligible landlord and tenant claims under Alberta residential-tenancy legislation.
records.population_served: Landlords and tenants with a dispute within RTDRS jurisdiction
records.eligibility: The dispute must fall within RTDRS jurisdiction and applicable filing limits. Filing fees and limitation periods apply unless an official fee-waiver route is available.
records.access_pathway: Review jurisdiction and filing requirements, prepare evidence and apply through the official RTDRS process.

housing.restrictions: Jurisdiction, filing and limitation requirements apply

legal_support.representation: The service decides eligible disputes; it does not provide a lawyer or act as a party's advocate.

records.name: Legal Aid Saskatchewan
records.description: Application pathway for covered criminal, family, immigration and other legal matters for people who meet Saskatchewan legal-aid criteria.
records.population_served: People whose financial circumstances and legal matter meet current Saskatchewan legal-aid rules
records.eligibility: Financial eligibility, the type of issue and the merits or coverage rules for the matter are assessed during application.
records.access_pathway: Call the Application Centre, request a callback, or contact a Legal Aid office to apply.

legal_support.representation: Representation is available only after an application is approved under current eligibility and coverage rules.

source.title: How do I apply for Legal Aid?

records.name: Free Legal Clinics
records.description: Up to one hour of free legal advice from a volunteer lawyer through clinics across Saskatchewan for eligible people with low incomes.
records.population_served: Saskatchewan residents with low incomes who meet the clinic's current appointment criteria
records.service_area: Saskatchewan through 17 listed clinic locations and telephone appointments
records.eligibility: The applicant must meet the clinic's low-income and appointment criteria.
records.access_pathway: Use the eligibility and appointment link on the clinic page or call the toll-free line.

legal_support.representation: The clinic provides advice during the appointment and does not take on full representation of the file.

records.name: CLASSIC Legal Clinics
records.organization: Community Legal Assistance Services for Saskatoon's Inner City
records.description: Case-by-case legal advocacy and brief advice for people experiencing poverty and injustice, including tenancy, social-assistance, human-rights and some criminal matters.
records.population_served: People who meet CLASSIC's case-by-case eligibility policies; some criminal or family matters require a prior Legal Aid denial
records.service_area: Saskatoon and telephone-based access as offered by the program
records.eligibility: Eligibility is assessed case by case. Criminal and family applicants must first be denied Legal Aid before applying for certain CLASSIC services.
records.access_pathway: Call CLASSIC to apply for the Walk-In Advocacy Clinic or a Legal Advice Clinic appointment.

legal_support.representation: Full representation may be available through the Walk-In Advocacy Clinic after staff approval; brief advice does not include full representation.

records.name: Office of Residential Tenancies Dispute Resolution
records.description: Official information, application and hearing process for residential landlord and tenant disputes in Saskatchewan.
records.population_served: Landlords and tenants with a matter within Saskatchewan residential-tenancy jurisdiction
records.eligibility: The matter must fall within the Office of Residential Tenancies' jurisdiction and filing rules.
records.access_pathway: Review the dispute and hearing steps, try direct resolution where appropriate, and file through the official process if needed.

housing.restrictions: Residential-tenancy jurisdiction and filing rules apply

legal_support.representation: The office provides process information and adjudicates eligible disputes; it does not represent either party.

source.title: Dispute Resolution and the Hearing Process

records.name: Canadian Human Rights Complaint Navigation
records.description: Official screening and intake information for discrimination complaints involving federally regulated organizations or federal services.
records.population_served: People with a complaint that may fall within federal Canadian Human Rights Act jurisdiction
records.service_area: Canada-wide for matters within federal jurisdiction
records.eligibility: The complaint must fall within federal human-rights jurisdiction and meet current filing requirements. Intake or acceptance is not a merits finding.
records.access_pathway: Use the Commission's eligibility questions and official complaint process; provincial or territorial matters may need a different human-rights body.

legal_support.representation: The Commission administers and screens complaints; it does not provide private legal representation.
